title: 3-Read Friday #46: Changing Minds, Shame, and Routines
author: Craig Barton
summary: This issue is built around the practical machinery of school culture: coaching, staffroom judgment, and September routines. Barton opens by introducing Sarah Cottinghatt's debut Cognitive Coaching newsletter post on how coaches help teachers change their mental models of practice, calling Cottinghatt one of his favourite thinkers and predicting the newsletter will become must-read. He follows with Jo Castelino's post on staffroom shame, which contrasts how quick teachers can be to judge a colleague's misconception against the patience they show a student's, a comparison Barton says made him reflect on his own reactions. He closes with Jo Morgan's rundown of the start-of-year routines her maths department uses for everything from classroom entry to parental communication, noting it has value well beyond maths teachers.
points: Barton personally vouches for Cottinghatt as one of his favourite thinkers in education, a strong editorial endorsement for a debut newsletter post.
He highlights Castelino's argument that teachers extend more patience to a student's misconception than to a colleague's, and admits it prompted self-reflection.
He recommends Morgan's routines post beyond its maths-teacher audience, flagging its relevance to whole-school communication and student support systems.
The throughline connects coaching, staffroom culture, and classroom routines as three different levers on the same goal: a more functional teaching culture.
